name: SCN4A (HYPP)
summary: SCN4A, hyperkalemic periodic paralysis (HYPP) - a dominant disorder of the muscle sodium channel, so one copy affects the horse and there is no silent carrier. The variant is c.4248C>G (p.Phe1416Leu; g.15474228C>G on chromosome 11, EquCab3.0). It causes episodes of muscle weakness or paralysis. The variant traces to the Quarter Horse stallion Impressive and is found in Quarter Horses and related breeds among his descendants. A horse with two copies is viable and typically more severely affected.

phenotypes.name: Wild type
phenotypes.description: Two working copies. Nothing is wrong and nothing is passed on.

phenotypes.name: HYPP (periodic paralysis)
phenotypes.description: A sodium-channel defect of muscle. One copy is enough: the horse has episodes of hyperkalemic periodic paralysis, in which the muscle locks up outside its control.

phenotypes.name: HYPP (two copies)
phenotypes.description: Two copies of the defect. The horse is viable and has the same episodes, typically more severely than a horse with one copy.
